subject: Latency contract qualification + live demo scheduling
messages:
From: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Ortiz <elena@orchidhealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 13 Nov 2026 15:10:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-demo notes — latency targets and next steps

Hi Elena — thanks again for the call earlier. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have the latency/throughput criteria captured for contracting and the live demo run: 

Primary acceptance targets (your asks)
- End-to-end p95: 350 ms (99th percentile target: 900 ms) — measured at the application edge (after our LB, through model, back to client).
- Throughput: sustained 420 QPS per region during business-hours traffic peaks (burst to 900 QPS tolerated for <5m).
- Streaming: support for 8 concurrent streaming sessions per agent seat with partial-response latency <60ms between tokens.
- Concurrency: baseline concurrency per requestor — 12 parallel requests per service account, scaleable to 40 for short bursts.

Key questions for contract/SLA drafting (please confirm):
1) Are p95/p99 targets measured with the same request distribution we demo'd (70% short prompts ~80–120 tokens, 30% long prompts 500–1,100 tokens)?
2) Is the acceptable fallback behavior (if hosted capacity constrained) to fall back to a quantized model variant with documented quality delta, or do you require queueing?
3) Will Orchid provide a representative traffic replay or can we run synthetic traffic using the attached test harness?

Proposed next steps: 
- You share the traffic profile CSV (samples you mentioned) + any retained session semantics (e.g., KV cache usage) — we can use it to run our on-pad proof (see redwood-test-plan.md attached).
- Redwood runs a controlled live demo next Tue/Wed window (30–45m): we execute 3 runs — baseline, burst, and streaming-heavy — and capture p95/p99 and token-cost numbers.
- We deliver an SLO acceptance worksheet (SLO-acceptance-template.xlsx attached) for signatures and contract language.

Can you confirm the p95/p99 numbers above (350 / 900) are still the goal for the contract? Also flag if you want the demo to exercise any specific integrations (client-side SDK vs server-side proxy).

Thanks — I’ll tentatively hold Tue 17th 10:00–10:45 PT for a live run if that works.

—
Logan Wright
Enterprise AE | Redwood Inference
log an.wright@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0126

Attachment: SLO-acceptance-template.xlsx (spreadsheet, 12KB)
From: Elena Ortiz <elena@orchidhealth.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.ai>
Cc: ops+infra@orchidhealth.com
Date: Fri, 13 Nov 2026 17:23:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo notes — latency targets and next steps

Hi Logan — thanks for capturing this crisply. Confirming items from our side: 

- Yes, the 350ms p95 and 900ms p99 are the upper bounds we need for the primary clinical inference path (client -> proxy -> model -> client). For background, our current provider averages p95=410ms and p99 ~1.2s during peak; those are the numbers we need to improve on or match.
- Traffic profile attached (orchid_latency_profile.csv) — includes timestamped replay for 48h, token distro, and a breakdown of streaming vs request/response flows.
- For fallback behavior, we prefer an explicit documented variant (quantized) with acceptance criteria (we’ll accept up to a 6% degradation on the NLU benchmark if you supply the eval). Queueing is a non-starter for our UX.

Quick clarifying points: 
- Streaming concurrency: the 8 concurrent sessions is per clinician session. Peak concurrent clinicians = ~220 across our west region; please validate how that maps to total streaming session capacity.
- For the demo, we can provide a temporary API key and a scoped test environment. Ops team (ops+infra) will coordinate TLS certs and access.

Proposed time: Tue 17 Nov 10:00 PT works; we’ll send a calendar invite once Ben confirms the test plan.

Thanks — Elena
Elena Ortiz
Head of Platform Engineering, Orchid Health
elena@orchidhealth.com | +1 (617) 555-0189

Attachment: orchid_latency_profile.csv (CSV, 38KB)
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Ortiz <elena@orchidhealth.com>, Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.ai>
Cc: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 14 Nov 2026 08:04:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo notes — latency targets and next steps

Elena — appreciate the data. Quick notes from the engineering side and what we’ll exercise during the live run: 

Planned test matrix (high-level):
- Baseline pass: replay orchard_profile at nominal QPS (420) with your standard prompt mix; measure edge p95/p99, CPU/GPU utilization, and token cost.
- Burst pass: short 5-minute bursts to 900 QPS to validate autoscale and tail behavior.
- Streaming pass: 220 concurrent clinician sessions mapped to 8 streams per clinician (we’ll run scaled-down mapping in the demo; full-scale run recommended in a later PI test).
- Cache/kv pass: we’ll exercise prefix caching for repeated context to show delta in token-cost and latency.

Notes / asks: 
1) Please confirm whether your proxy pins persistent connections (we can benefit from HTTP/2 multiplexing) or your client opens single-shot connections — that changes our tail-latency profile.
2) We’ll need a short list of 6–8 representative prompts for the streaming demo (varied lengths). If you prefer, Redwood can use anonymized samples from your CSV.
3) To validate p99 in the demo window we’ll capture 10M tokens across runs; this gives us statistical confidence for p99 <-> contractual commitments.

I’ve attached the Redwood test plan (redwood-test-plan.md) — it’s intentionally short. If you confirm the connection behavior and give us the token samples, we’ll finalize the runbook and push a calendar invite.

—
Ben Carter
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.ai

Attachment: redwood-test-plan.md (markdown, 4KB)

Confirming the proxy behavior: we use HTTP/2 persistent connections from our server-side proxy, but client-side mobile apps sometimes open single-shot connections. For the demo, please optimize for persistent server-side connections (that’s the path we care most about).

I’ve added six anonymized prompt samples to a folder in the Drive link below and shared a scoped API key for the demo environment (ops will DM the key to Logan). I’ll send an ICS invite for Tue 17 10:00 PT; attaching the invite for your calendar.
